prize_parts.citation: for developing targeted protein degradation, using small molecules to bring a chosen protein to the cell's own ubiquitin ligase machinery for destruction

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation rests on one clear, transferable principle: a small molecule that induces proximity between an E3 ligase and a target converts occupancy-driven pharmacology into event-driven, catalytic removal of the protein. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the bifunctional PROTAC concept, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains molecular glue degraders and links the two lineages under one citation. The field is generative in the sense I care about: it opens targets once called undruggable and has been independently reproduced with structures, mechanism and many clinical-stage compounds. Four of eight members placed it in their top three, the broadest support among the shortlist. I moved it above base editing, my opening first choice, because that support is broader and the attribution is cleaner for a three-person prize than my Liu, Komor, Gaudelli proposal.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity: no PROTAC drug is approved, so clinical proof of the PROTAC branch is incomplete, and the committee has to be sure it is rewarding the principle and not the pipeline. Attribution is also genuinely lossy: Ciulli (rational VHL ligand design), Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito all made real contributions, and a three-person cut excludes them. Finally, the glue and PROTAC lineages are historically distinct, and a joint citation may blur what was actually discovered by whom.

responses.point: Aili ranks PROTACs first and proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa, accepting that the clinical record is incomplete and that a three-person prize leaves out real credit.
responses.response: I now agree with his configuration and his reading of the principle. Where I press him is the Handa inclusion: cereblon explains glue degraders but is not the PROTAC concept, so the citation must name the shared principle, induced proximity to a ubiquitin ligase, rather than list two stories. I also do not think the incomplete clinical record should count heavily against it, since the discovery is the mechanism, which is already independently validated.

responses.point: Chabes ranks sequencing-by-synthesis first for Balasubramanian and Klenerman, citing exceptional maturity, overdue recognition and a chemical innovation (reversible terminators) that reshaped genomics.
responses.response: I take the maturity argument seriously and I keep B055 as an alternative. My qualification is attribution: the shortlist credits Rothberg and Mayer on parallel platforms, so a two-person Cambridge prize would have to defend excluding 454 pyrosequencing, which is a priority and fairness fight I would want resolved before preferring it. I also ask whether the citation is chemistry or enabling instrumentation. Overdue is not by itself a reason to put it first this year.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Car-Parrinello first, arguing that the two-person credit is unambiguous, priority is clean and four decades of use make recognition overdue.
responses.response: I accept that the attribution for B007 is the cleanest on the list and that it fits the demanded standard of a simple idea that changed a field. My reservation is about breadth of benefit: it is a method whose success is partly in enabling calculations, and only one other member ranked it in the top five, so I do not see a majority forming. I would like him to say what a one-sentence citation to a general audience would be, and whether the chemical outcomes, not just the algorithm, carry it.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular condensates first as a physical-chemical reframing of intracellular organization, based on phase behaviour, valency and interfacial thermodynamics.
responses.response: As a physicist I find the framework appealing and ranked B063 third. My concern is the one I raised on maturity: the physiological relevance and material state of many reported condensates are still debated, and I worry that a prize now would freeze a concept whose boundaries are not settled. Her point that Rosen's multivalency work supplies the quantitative principle is persuasive, but I would ask whether the discovery separates cleanly from the later, broader claims about condensate function.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling first, emphasizing its generality, daily use in pharmaceutical synthesis and full maturity.
responses.response: I agree that Buchwald-Hartwig is mature and important and that the ligand design is a real contribution. My qualification is novelty of principle relative to the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which I would expect others on the committee to see as a refinement of a recognized area, and the Kosugi precursor complicates priority. I would like to hear his view on whether the argument for it rests on a new capability or on scale of use.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a combined PROTAC and molecular glue citation, or whether one lineage should be the focus.
Whether the lack of an approved PROTAC drug makes recognition premature for this year.
How to weigh Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito against the three-person limit.
Whether the committee judges base editing (B021) to be ahead of protein degradation once Liu-only attribution is considered.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile: I am at Lund University, as are fellow committee members Somfai and Sparr, but none of the shortlisted candidates is identified as a Lund colleague or collaborator in my profile, and my own work (nanowire thermoelectrics and molecular motors) does not overlap with any shortlisted topic.
